```{r}
# path to data shp

mal_2020_path <- "./data/shp/malaria_2020_selected.shp"

# read in data

```

```{r}
# list column names
mal_2015 %>%
  colnames()
```
```{r}
library(brms)
```

```{r}
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Spatial Model with brms
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

# Centering the coordinates, often recommended for numerical stability in spatial models
brms_data <- mal_2015 %>%
  mutate(
    LATNUM_c = LATNUM - mean(LATNUM),
    LONGNUM_c = LONGNUM - mean(LONGNUM)
  )
```

```{r}
# Define the brms formula
formula_brms <- bf(
  parasitaemia_prop ~ 1 +
    paste(covariate_names, collapse = " + "),
  # Spatial component using Gaussian process
  +gp(LATNUM_c, LONGNUM_c,
    # cov = "exp_quad", # You can choose a different covariance function
    # The line below is crucial for allowing brms to handle  the zero-inflated beta
    # family correctly.  It tells brms that the predictors also affect the
    # probability of a zero.
    autocor = TRUE
  ),
  # Set the distribution.
  family = zero_inflated_beta()
)
```

```{r}
# Priors (adjust as needed) - VERY IMPORTANT
priors_brms <- c(
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = "Intercept"), # Intercept prior
  prior(normal(0, 0.5), class = "b", coef = all_of(covariate_names)), # Covariate priors
  prior(exponential(10), class = "sdgp"), # Prior for spatial SD
  prior(exponential(10), class = "lengthscale"), # Prior for spatial range
  prior(beta(1, 1), class = "zi") # Prior for zero-inflation parameter.  alpha = 1, beta = 1 is uniform.
)

# Fit the model with brms
#   Use a reasonable number of chains and iterations.  Adjust 'cores' as needed.
brms_model <- brm(
  formula = formula_brms,
  data = brms_data,
  prior = priors_brms,
  chains = 4,
  iter = 2000,
  cores = 4,
  control = list(
    adapt_delta = 0.95,
    max_treedepth = 12
  ), # Increase these if you get warnings
  # file = "your_model_file.rds" #Save the model to a file.  Useful for large models.
)

# Save the model
saveRDS(brms_model, file = "parasitaemia_model_brms.rds")

# Print a summary of the model
print(summary(brms_model))
```
